properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 16 at 4:14AM PST until November 16 at 9:00PM PST by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10
to 15 feet increasing to 15 to 18 feet with local sets to 20
feet. Dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
minor coastal flooding expected.

* WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara
County Central Coast Beaches.

* WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 3 PM PST Tuesday. For
the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 9 PM PST this evening.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk for ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Large breaking waves can
cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize
small boats near shore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The High Surf Advisory may need to be
extended through Wednesday, and another round of larger surf
is expected Thursday into Friday.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to dangerous surf conditions, or stay
near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly in
such conditions, stay off the rocks.

properties.areaDesc: South End of the Upper Sierra
properties.headline: Winter Storm Watch issued November 16 at 3:40AM PST until November 20 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Hanford CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Heavy snow possible Above 5, 000 feet. Total snow
accumulations 6 to 12 inches above this level; accumulations 2 to 3
feet above 8,000 feet. Winds could gust as high as 35 mph.

* WHERE...South End of the Upper Sierra above 5,000 feet.

* WHEN...From late Tuesday night through late Thursday night.

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The
hazardous conditions will impact daily travel. Gusty winds could
bring down tree branches. Roads, and especially bridges and
overpasses, will likely become slick and hazardous.
properties.instruction:
Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

Persons are urged to stay indoors until conditions improve. If you
must go outside, dress in layers. Several layers of clothes will keep
you warmer than a single heavy coat. Cover exposed skin to reduce
your risk of frostbite or hypothermia. Gloves, a scarf, and a hat
will keep you from losing your body heat.

Persons should consider delaying all travel. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution. Consider taking a winter storm
kit along with you, including such items as tire chains, booster
cables, flashlight, shovel, blankets and extra clothing. Also take
water, a first aid kit, and anything else that would help you survive
in case you become stranded.

* WHERE...Elevations above 3500 ft in Siskiyou County, including
Highway 89 at Snowman Summit and Dead Horse Summit, Highway 3 at

* WHEN...From Tuesday evening through late Wednesday night. Heavy

* IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult to impossible. The

properties.instruction:
Monitor the latest forecasts for updates on this situation.

Persons should delay all travel if possible. If travel is absolutely
necessary, drive with extreme caution and be prepared for sudden
changes in visibility. Leave plenty of room between you and the
motorist ahead of you, and allow extra time to reach your
destination. Avoid sudden braking or acceleration, and be especially
cautious on hills or when making turns. Make sure your car is
winterized and in good working order.
